paragraphs: On Monday at lunch, Tom and Ben sat under a big tree at school. Ben had a small box and a phone. "What is in the box?" asked Tom. "It is clay," said Ben. "I make films with it, and it is my hobby." "How do you make a film with clay?" asked Tom. "I make a small clay man," said Ben. "After I take a photo, I move the man a little." "Then I take another photo."

"How many photos do you need?" asked Tom. "For a short film, I need a thousand photos," said Ben. "My last film took two weeks." "A thousand!" said Tom. "That is a lot of work." "Yes, but I like it," said Ben. "If I move the man a little, he looks like a real boy." "Why do you like it?" asked Tom. "I think of the story, and it is my film," said Ben. "A good story is important to me."

"Is it expensive?" asked Tom. "No, it is cheap," said Ben. "The clay is cheap, and my phone is old." "I only need time." "Have you ever made a film for the class?" asked Tom. "Twice," said Ben. "Teacher Nick showed my first film to his class, and they asked for it again."

Then Ben opened his bag and took out a green card. "This is an invitation," he said. "Please visit me on Saturday." The card had a drawing of a clay man, and it said, "Film afternoon. Saturday, two o'clock." "Bring Lily too," said Ben. "She can write a story for my next film." "Yes, I can ask her," said Tom.

Tom looked at the card for a long time. "I have never made a film," he said. "Then Saturday is a good day to start," said Ben. Tom put the card in his bag very carefully. He was excited, because it was his first invitation from Ben.
